title: PAGELATCH_EX on the last page of PK_Orders during the flash sale
prompt: Azure SQL Database 'RetailOps', General Purpose, 8 vCores, about 41.5 GB of memory, compatibility level 160, no readable secondary. Snapshot taken Thursday 2026-09-24 09:00 UTC. A platform failover reset the index usage counters on 2026-09-15 02:41, so they cover 9.26 days. Query Store holds data from 2026-09-11 only, because size-based cleanup has run. Month-end change freeze: 2026-09-30 18:00 to 2026-10-02 18:00. Flash sale on 2026-10-09 with a change freeze from 2026-10-08. Log rate cap: 36 MB/s. Space headroom: 213 GB.
Ticket from the platform team: 'Before the Autumn Sale, stop the order-insert slowdowns we saw on 09-19.' Decide what
to change on PK_Orders, and whether PK_InventoryMovement needs the same change.

workload.description: INSERT dbo.Orders (marketplace importer and web checkout, single-row inserts)
workload.plan: Clustered Index Insert PK_Orders plus 8 nonclustered indexes.

facts: Flash sale 2026-09-19 18:00-21:00: PAGELATCH_EX was 61% of wait time. Up to 180 sessions waited on one page: PK_Orders, level 0, the last page of the index. All of them ran Q6.
Q6 went from 2.1 ms to 410 ms; the importer timed out and retried. CPU peaked at 61%. Peak 900 inserts per second from about 220 sessions.
PK_Orders: page_latch_wait_count 4.1M, page_latch_wait_in_ms 2,950,000, most of it in that window.
dbo.InventoryMovement: 12 writers, one per warehouse, each sending 500-row batches. PK_InventoryMovement page_latch_wait_count is 3,200.
The service tier is General Purpose.

decisions.why: The contention is a latch convoy on the last page of an ever-increasing key. The option is a metadata-only change that keeps the key.
Twelve batched writers do not contend: 3,200 latch waits in nine days.

must_not_create.why: A GUID, reversed or hashed clustered key trades the latch for fragmentation and page splits on a 182M-row table and rebuilds eight nonclustered indexes.

harmful_removals.why: It is the primary key and the clustered index of the table.
